title: Pressure prediction of phase stability, anisotropic elasticity, and thermodynamic properties of <scp>Ti<sub>2</sub>AC</scp> (<scp>A = Cd, In</scp>) ternary compound
abstract: AbstractIn this study, the effects of high pressure on phase stability, anisotropic elasticity, and thermodynamic properties of Ti2AC (A = Cd, In) were predicted by using first‐principles based on density functional theory. The negative formation enthalpy indicates that Ti2AC (A = Cd, In) is thermodynamically stable at pressures of 0–50 GPa. The elastic constants and polycrystalline moduli of Ti2AC (A = Cd, In) increase with increasing pressure, while its elastic anisotropies decrease with increasing pressure. The density of states demonstrates that no phase transition occurs in the pressure range 0–50 GPa. In addition, the influences of high pressure (up to 50 GPa) and temperature (up to 2000 K) on the thermodynamic properties of Ti2AC (A = Cd, In) were systematically studied based on the quasi‐harmonic Debye model. Finally, the sound velocities and minimum thermal conductivities are also discussed.
